ORAL ANSWERS TO QUESTIONS 
Sale of reliance shares to fake firms. 
*181.   SHRI JIBON ROY: † 
SHRI SANJAY NIRUPAM: 
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government are aware th at Reliance Infocomm has sold a 
total of one crore preferentia l shares to three fake firms at the rate of Rs. one 
each; and 
(b) if so, whether Government would insitute an enquiry on the whole 
affair? 
THE MINISTER OF FINANCE (SH. P. CHIDAMBARAM) (a) and (b) A 
Statement is placed on the Table of the House. 
Statement 
(a) and (b) According to information furnished by the Ministry of 
Company Affairs, three unlisted companie s held shares in an unlisted public 
limited company by name Reliance Infocomm Limited (Registration No. 04-
21441).  
†The question was actually asked on the floor of the House by Shri Jibon 
Roy. 
4 

[15 March, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
The shares were acquired by each of the three companies on 12.9.2002 from 
three persons (K.R. Raja, C.S. Mo ghe and V.K. Gandhi). The three 
companies and their shareholdings are: 
1. M/s. Prerana Auto Private Limited 33,00,000 shares 
2. M/s. Softnet Traders & Consultants 33,00,000 shares 
Private Limited 
3. M/s. Fairever Traders & Consultants 34,00,000 shares 
Private Limited 
By an order of the High Court of Gujarat dated 16.12.2002, Reliance 
Infocomm Limited (Registration No. 04-21441) was amalgamated with M/s. 
Reliance Information and Communications Limited, another unlisted 
company (Registration NO. 04-41035). Upon amalgamation the name of the 
amalgamated company was changed to  Reliance Infocomm Limited, but 
continued to carry the registration no. 04-41035. 
The three shareholding companies re ferred to above were issued new 
shares by the amalgamated company in replacement of the old shares held by 
them. The swap ratio was 1:1. Consequently, the three companies held the 
following shares in the amalgamated company (Registration No. 04-41035). 
1. M/s. Prerana Auto Private Limited 33,00,000 shares 
2. M/s. Softnet Traders & Consultants 33,00,000 shares 
Private Limited 
3. M/s. Fairever Traders & Consultants 34,00,000 shares 
Private Limited 
From the available Balance Sheets of the three companies, as at 
31.3.2004, the price at which the th ree companies acquired share in the 
erstwhile Reliance Infocomm Limited (Regn. No. 04-21441) appears to be at 
Re 1 per share. When these shares were  substituted by new shares issued by 
the amalgamated company (Regn. No. 04-41035) no further price was paid. 
The three companies were shown as shareholders of the amalgamated 
company (Regn. No. 04-41035) in the Annual Return filed by the 
amalgamated company on 27.9.2003 and 23.9.2004. 
According to the information provided by National Securities Depository 
Limited (NSDL), each of the three companies transferred its entire share 
5 

RAJYA SABHA [15 March, 2005] 
holding in the amlgamated company (Regn. No. 04-41035) on 11.2.2005 in 
favour of Ganesh Infrstructure Fund, which appers to be a Trust. 
Since the three companies have filed their Balance sheets as at 31.3.2004, 
they are working companies. 
SHRI JIBON ROY: Sir, the hon. Minister has confirmed that on 12th 
September, 2002, RIC has transferred one crore of preferential shares to three 
insignificant companies. They may tran sfer, there is no problem in it. But 
they have transferred it at a price of Re . 1 per share when the market price at 
that time was around Rs. 250 each. Th erefore, it looks that through the 
transfer, Rs. 250 crores was transferred to three insignificant companies. 
MR. CHAIRMAN: What is your question? 
SHRI JIBON ROY: Sir, it appears that there is a fishy game behind it. It 
was a gift and not a transfer in the real sense. Would the Ministry of Finance 
inquire into the matter and institute a high-power inquiry to find out the 
interest in both the sides—those who have transferred and those who got it? 
CHAIRMAN: You have put your question and let the Minister reply. 
(Interruptions) Please take your seat. 
SHRI P. CHIDAMBARAM: Sir, as I have stated in the answer, Reliance 
Infocomm Limited, that is the erstwhile company with Registration No. 04-
21441, was an unlisted public limited company. This company issued the 
shares to three entities which I have mentioned in my answer. This company 
was amalgamated with Reliance Information and Communication Limited 
with Registration No. 04-41035 and this also is an unlisted company. 
Unlisted companies don't fall under the jurisdiction of SEBI and, they are 
not, therefore, governed by the SEBI regulations. The Directors and the 
General Body of an unlisted company are, under the law as it stands today, 
free to allocate shares to anyone as long as appropriate resolutions are passed. 
It is after looking into the matter that I have gathered, the hon. Member will 
agree, a large amount of information, and I have placed it on the Table of the 
House. But we are looking into the matter to see if there is any law that has 
been violated. At the moment, I am not in a position to say that any law has 
been violated. 
SHRI JIBON ROY: Mr. Chairman, Sir, the news of the interesting 
development has come to the Press also, the prior to 12th September, 2002, 
Reliance Infocomm violated the standards of technology prescribed

is a matter, on which I am sure, hon. Member can put a question to the

SHRI JIBON ROY: It has caused a loss to the exchequer.

MR. CHAIRMAN: Please take your seat .......... (Interruptions)... Let him

A statement is placed on the Table of the House. 
Statement 
(a) to (d) VAT is a State level tax reform measure which is proposed to be 
implemented by States in lieu of the existing Sales Tax system: An 
Empowered Committee of State Finance Ministers has been set up to decide 
on all issues relating to implementation of State Level VAT. 
The Empowered Committee of State Fi nance Ministers, in its meeting 
held on 17th January, 2005, has decided that for the year 2005-06, tea could 
be taxed at 4% under the VAT regime. As the existing rate of Sale Tax on tea 
in most of the States is 4% or more, it is not likely that prices of tea will rise 
as a consequence of introduction of VAT. 
SHRI K. CHANDRAN PILLAI: Sir, from the answer it is clear that under 
the VAT regime, the sales tax for tea will be 4 per cent. There was an 
apprehension that it would be 12.5 per cent. Now, it is unambiguous through

last sentence of his answer he has said, "There is no possibility for price rise 
of tea". But I would like to seek a clarification from the hon. Minister, what is

below 4 per cent? If, 'yes', there is potential possibility for price rise. Also, if 
there is above 4 per cent in any State, there is possibility of loss of their 
resources also through this tax. Do you contemplate to have any scheme 
under the new regime to compensate that? 
SHRI P. CHIDAMBARAM: Mr. Chairman, Sir, I think we must remove 
these misconceptions about VAT. Regardless of political party affiliation, 
regardless of who was in charge in the Central Government or the State 
Governments, every political party in this  country, over the last seven years 
has worked with other political parties and evolved a consensus on VAT. The 
benefits of VAT have been explained. A white paper has been published. We 
must also respect the decision of th e State Finance Ministers belonging to 
different political parties. But there are one or two things which I wish to 
clarify before I give the information on tax on tea. 
VAT is a State tax. It is not a tax which Parliament imposes or the Central 
Government imposes. VAT is intended to substitute the sales tax of the State. 
Both the sales tax as well as the new VAT fall under Entry 54 of List II. All 
the State Finance Ministers have laboured through seven years, under three 
different Prime Ministers, and have come to the 
16

conclusion that VAT must be introduced and they have set the date as 1st 
April. Now tea was a sticking point because the Empowered Committee of 
State Finance Ministers had initially recommended that tea will be taxed at 
the higher of the two rates, namely, 12.5 per cent. Some States, of course, 
pointed out that this would be detrimental to their interests. Why? Assam 
today has an 8 per cent sales tax rate on tea. Kerala has a 4 per cent rate. 
Tamil Nadu has, for general sale, 8 per cent plus a 5 per cent surcharge 
making it 8.4 per cent. For tea sold through tea auction centres, it is 4 per 
cent. In West Bengal, it is 8 per cent plus a 15 per cent surcharge making it 
9.2 per cent. So, you will notice, Sir, that the range is between 4—9.2 per 
cent. Having regard to the structur e, the Empowered Committee of State 
Finance Ministers met once again and decided that tea will not be taxed under 
VAT at 12.5 per cent, it will be taxed at 4 per cent. These four States-are 
parties to that decision. Therefore, t ea will be taxed at 4 per cent under VAT 
as per the decision taken by the Empowered Committee of State Finance 
Ministers.

A Statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
Statement 
(a to d) The Task Force has inter alia suggested that if the cooperatives

* Special financial assistance of  Rs. 14,839 crore to wipe out

Co-operative Credit Structures. 
• Qualitative improvement in personnel in all tiers and at all levels. 
• State Governments need to make le gislative amendments to enable 
RBI to exercise its, regulatory powers under the Banking Regulation 
Act. The Task Force has su,. jest ed the working draft of a Model 
Cooperative Law.

revival package. The Scheme be kept open for a period of two years 
for the State Governments to decide on the participation and may be 
closed for such purposes on 31st March, 2008. Release of funds 
should be linked to the progress by the State Government in actually 
implementing the revival package.

• Since legislative amendments may take time, the State Governments

commercial banks as far as regulatory norms are concerned.

(a) whether the investigation by the CBI into stamp paper scam has been 
completed; 
(b) if so, the outcome of the enquiry; 
(c) how many people have been charged for this so far, name-wise details 
with charges framed; and 
(d) value of fake stamps/stamp paper seized till date? 
THE MINISTER OF FINANCE (SHRI P. CHIDAMBARAM): (a) to (d) 
A Statement is laid on the Table of the House. 
(a) CBI has informed that it has re gistered 64 cases out of which 
investigation in 20 cases have been completed and remaining 44 cases are 
pending at different stages of investigation. 
31 

RAJYA SABHA [15 March, 2005] 
(b) and (c) CBI's investigations in the 64 cases has resulted in filing 
charge sheets against 149 accused pe rsons so far. Some accused have 
been charge sheeted in more than one case. The name-wise"details with 
charges are indicated in Annexure.  
[See Appendix 2004 Annexure No. 13] 
(d) Fake Stamp Papers of the value of Rs. 3396 crores (approx.) have been 
seized so far. 
SHRI SHAHID SIDDIQUI: Sir, the Mini ster has said that the value of 
fake stamp papers recovered is Rs. 3396 crores. At the height of this scandal, 
it was being alleged that the scandal was to the tune of Rs. 30,000 crores or 
even 60,000 crores. 
I would like to know from the Minister whether the Government has made 
any investigation to know as to what exactly is the amount, which was 
involved in this scandal because it has implications on our economy and lot 
of common people have suffered because of this. What exactly is the 
position? Secondly, the investigation has been slow. According to the reply, 
investigation has been completed only in 20 cases and 44 cases are still 
pending. I would like to know as to what steps are being taken to expedite the 
investigation. 
SHRI P. CHIDAMBARAM: Sir, while the scam was a major scandal and 
a great scam, I don't think we should say anything, which could spread any 
kind of alarm among the people. My predecessor has assured this House and 
the people that no document will become invalid merely because the 
executant or the receiver finds later that  it was a spurious document. Sir, we 
are in touch with the Stat es. No State has so far asked for any legislative 
changes. I will honour my predecessor's word, and if  it becomes necessary, I 
will take suitable administrative and legislative steps. But, so far, no 
document has been set-aside on the ground that it was subsequently 
discovered to be spurious. 
Sir, I don't know the size of the scan dal. That can only be discovered by 
investigation and the investigation so far reveals that the scandal was 
widespread and it was spread over many States. Prosecution is taking place in 
many States. In 20 cases the investigation has been completed and in 44 cases 
the investigation is under progress. As and when more people are found to be 
involved. I am sure that CBI will take action. I will certainly ask for 
periodical reports from CBI about the progress of the cases.

SHRI P. CHIDAMBARAM: Sir, there are 130 bank accounts operated by 
Abdul Karim Telgi and his associates. In order to protect the interest of 
revenue, the Income Tax Department has made a provisional attachment of 
movable and immovable properties of Abdul Karim Telgi, his family 
members and his associates. Till date, the department has attached 51 
movable and 67 immovable properties at Mumbai, Kanpur and Bangalore. To 
ascertain the market value of the properties, the matter has been referred to 
the Evaluation Cell. The department has auctioned one property at Bangalore 
for a value of Rs. 1.43 crores. 
Pursuant to the notices issued by the department, Abdul Karim Telgi filed 
his tax returns for the assessment years from 1996-97 to 2002-03 declaring a 
total income of Rs. 2.89 crores in the years under consideration. These 
returns are under examination. On th e basis of evidence available, the 
department has completed the assessment for the assessment year 1996-97 
and has determined a total income of Rs. 4.09 crores as against the income of 
Rs. 38.35 lakhs shown in the return. Steps are under way to recover the 
amount of income tax. We have also invoked the penal provisions under the 
Income Tax Act.

Benefits of VAT 
*186. SHRI DARA SINGH: Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether Government have fully asse ssed benefits or disadvantages by 
VAT's introduction in the country from 1st April, 2005 and how far it is 
different from Central Sales Tax: 
(b) which are the States who have passed a VAT law till date and whether 
any State not willing to do so; 
(c) whether VAT will operate on the basis of uniform rates across the 
country by ending several State-level or vary in respect of unwilling State 
like Uttar Pradesh; and 
(d) what special relief small dealer s/traders will get under VAT whose 
turnover is up to 5 to 50 lakhs annually? 
THE MINISTER OF FINANCE (SHRI P. CHIDAMBARAM): (a) to (d) 
VAT is a State level tax reform measure, which is proposed to be 
implemented by States in lieu of the existing Sales Tax system. An 
Empowered Committee of State Finance Ministers has been set up to decide 
on all issues relating to implementation of State Level VAT. The Empowered 
44 

[15 March, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
Committee of State Finance Ministers has decided to implement VAT and 
has finalized the VAT design, after prolonged deliberations and due 
consideration of advantages offered by the VAT System. The State Level 
VAT being introduced from 1st April, 20 05 is different from Central Sales 
Tax, in the sense that while the former is on inter-State sales (i.e. sales within 
a State), the latter is on inter-State sales. 
A statement indicating the latest position with respect to the VAT 
Legislations of States/UTs is give n in the statement-l (See below). No 
State/UT has communicated its unwillingness to pass VAT Legislation. 
As decided by the Empowered Committee of State Finance Ministers, 
VAT will operate on the basis of uniform rates across the country. However, 
in case any State is not able to impl ement VAT w.e.f. 1st April, 2005, the 
existing system of sales tax shall continue in that State. Further, as decided 
by the Empowered Committee, it is expected that a number of State level 
taxes on purchase or sales of goods like state sales tax, turnover tax, purchase 
tax, additional sales tax, surcharge, entr y tax (not in lieu of octroi) etc. will 
be subsumed in VAT. 
Small dealers with annual turnover not exceeding Rs. 50 lakhs, who are 
otherwise liable to pay VAT, shall have the option for a compaistion scheme 
with payment of tax at a small percentage to turnover.

Appreciation of Rupee 
*188. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT: Will the Minister of FINANCE be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that rupee has appreciated considerably in relation 
to US $ during the past few months; 
(b) if so, the factors responsible for the same; and 
(c) its financial implications on the Indian economy? 
THE MINISTER OF FINANCE (SHRI P. CHIDAMBARAM): (a) and (b) 
The Rupee appreciated against the US Dollar by 6.1 per cent during the 
period September-February 2004-05. This appreciation has primarily been on 
account to higher supply of foreign ex change, compared to demend, arising 
out of foreign portfolio inflows, trade remittances, etc. against the backdrop 
of the weakness exhibited by US Dollar agaisnt other major currencies in the 
international market. 
(c) The movements in the Rupee value have been smooth and orderly, 
avoiding any significant costs to the economy. Both exports and imports have 
continued to post robust growth and, coupled with strong capital inflows, the 
overall balance of payments position remains comfortable. The foreign 
exchange reserves,which stood at US $ 113 billion at end-March 2004, have 
improved further, and are currently placed at US $ 135.7 billion, as on 
February, 25.2005.

India is the most attractive short term FDI destination of the world; 
(b) whether it is also a fact that India is going to beat markets like Brazil, 
Maxico, Poland etc, to become a great  market potential for mid-term FDI 
destinations of the world; 
(c) if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) what measures Government are cont emplating to make India the first 
or the second most attractive destination of the world from the present 3 rt 
position? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE (SHRI 
S.S. PALANIMANICKAM): (a) to (c ) Yes, Sir. According to FDI 
confidence Index 2004 survey of CEO conducted by AT Kearney, a Global 
management Consultancy Firm, India is the 3 rd most attractive destination in 
the World, after China and USA. 
Global Investors view India as the preferred investment destination 
because of India's capability as a business process,  IT Services provider and 
for R&D with long term market potential.

November, 2004 was US$ 3607 Million as compared to US$ 2363 Million 
during the corresponding period of the previous year. 
(d) To make the environment more attractive, Government has on 
September, 29,2004 further simplified the FDI approval procedure by 
placing the following on the automatic route; 
(i) Transfer of shares from resident to non-resident (including transfer of 
subscribers' shares to non-residents) other than in financial services sector 
provided the investment is covered und er automatic route, falls within the 
sectoral cap and also complies with prescribed pricing guidelines.

company is covered under automatic r oute, the foreign equity after such

shares as well as conversion of preferen ce shares into equity capital provided 
such increase falls within th e sectoral cap in the relevant sectors, are within

1458. SHRI B.K. HARIPRASAD: W ill the Minister of FINANCE be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether there is a growing trend in the circulation of forged currency 
through the banking channel; 
(b) if so, whether the Banks are not equi pped to identify forged currency; 
and 
(c) whether the Reserve Bank of India also receives forged currency 
through Bank remittances and if so , whether the RBI accepts them for 
repayment in genuine currency? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE (SHRI 
S.S. PALANIMANICKAM): (a) No, Sir. 
(b) and (c) RBI have issued instructions to Banks to equip their branches 
with Ultra Violet Lamps for detection of forged notes and to report to the 
police authorities in case of detection of counterfeit notes at their branches. 
Over 85% branches of Banks have in stalled the same. The currency chest 
holding Banks have also been advised to instal Note Sorting Machines at all 
the chests in a time-bound manner latest by November, 2005. 
Further, RBI has installed 48 Currency Verification and Processing 
Systems (CVPS) each having a processing capacity of 50,000 to 60,000 
pieces per hour. These machines have capacity to detect forged notes and 
also to sort notes into non-issuable  and re-issuable ones. RBI has advised 
banks to set up Forged Notes Vigilance Cells at their Head Offices for 
monitoring and implementation of RBI instructions on forged notes.

Introduction of VAT in the country 
1462. SHRI CHO.S. RAMASWAMY: Will the Minister of FINANCE be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that the Go vernment are intr oducing the VAT 
system all over the country from April, 2005; 
(b) if so, what are the special features of this scheme; 
(c) whether it will check the double taxation across the board; 
(d) what will be the benefits to th e common public through this VAT 
scheme; and 
(e) what will be the change in revenue collection if this process is 
implemented? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE (SHRI 
S.S. PALANIMANICKAM) (a) to (c) Value Added Tax is a State level tax 
reform measure which is proposed to be implemented by States in lieu of the 
existing Sales Tax system. The Central Government is playing the role of 
facilitator in this tax reform process.  VAT is a simple, transparent, multi-
stage tax with input tax credit, which e liminates cascading of taxes. Further, 
as decided by the Empowered Committ ee, it is expected that a number of 
State level taxes on purchase or sales of goods like State sales tax, turnover 
tax, purchase tax, additional sales tax, surcharge, entry tax (not in lieu of 
Octroi) will be sub-sumed in VAT. Henc e, instead of multiplicity of taxes, 
there would only be a single tax. 
(d) The provision of Input Tax Credit (ITC) is one of the most significant 
features of VAT which ensures that ther e is no cascading of tax (i.e.tax on 
tax) and no consequent price escalation which is ultimately beneficial to the 
common public.

However, actual impact on revenues of States/UTs shall be known only after 
VAT is actually implemented by the States/UTs.

RAJYA SABHA [15 March, 2005] 
Statement 
Recommendations of the first round table of Ministers-in-charge of 
PanchayatiRaj—Kolkata. 24-25th July, 2004  
Ministers in charge of Panchayati Raj and their representatives, bearing in 
mind the spirit of cooperative federalism which must inform the effective 
implementation of Panchayati Raj as set out in Para IX of the Constitution of 
India and related provisions, including in  particular, Article 243ZD (District 
Planning Committees), agreed to  recommend to their respective 
Governments, for joint acceptance by the Centre and the States, the following 
points of action:— Effective Devolution of Functions: 
(I) The Constitution (Article 243G) provides for "devolution", that is, 
the empowerment of Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs) to function as 
institutions of self-government for the twin purposes of (i) making plans for 
economic development and social justi ce for their respective areas, and (ii) 
implementing programmes of economic development and social justice in 
their respective areas, for subjects de volved to the PRIs, including those 
listed in the Eleventh Schedule, and subject to such conditions as the State 
may, by law, specify. Therefore, th e key objective is to ensure that 
Panchayati Raj Institutions function as in stitutions of self-government rather 
than as more implementing agencies for other authorities in respect of such 
functions as may be devolved on them; 
(II) While devolution must eventually  comprise the entire range of 
subjects provided for in the State legislation in a time-bound manner, States/ 
UTs may prioritize their devolution programme to ensure that for such 
functions as are prioritized, there is  full and effective devolution in 
empowering PRIs as institutions of se lf-government in respect of these 
functions; 
(HI) To this end, the essential step is the identification of activities related 
to the devolved functions with a view to attributing each of these activities to 
the appropriate tier of the 3-tier system. To the extent possible, there should 
be no overlapping between tiers in respect of any given activity; 
(IV) In determining the tier of the Panchayati Raj System to which any 
given activity is to be attributed, the principle of subsidiarity must, to the 
extent possible, be followed. The principle of subsidiarity states that any 
activity which can be undertaken at a lower level must be undertaken at that 
level in preference to being undertaken at any higher level; 
132 

[15 March, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
(V) On the basis of the identification of activities relating to devolved 
functions, and through the application of the principle of the subsidiarity, 
States/UTs may review/undertake time bound activity mapping with a view 
to completing this exercise within the fiscal year 2004-05; 
(VI) The activity mapping model as evolved in the Ministry of Rural 
Development in the Report of the Task Force on Devolution of Powers and 
Functions upon Panchayati Raj Institutions, and the information provided 
about existing State-wise activity mapping in the Fact Sheets presented to the 
Round Table, might be drawn upon by State Governments/UT 
Administrations for preparing their respective activity mapping exercises; 
(VII) The Union Ministry of Panchayati Raj could, on request, furnish 
technical assistance and expertise to State Govts./UT Administrations to 
accomplish activity mapping within the time-frame indicated. 
(VIII) With a view to promoting a measure of irrevocability of devolved 
functions, devolution may be routed through legislative measures or, 
alternatively, by providing a strong legislative framework for devolution 
through executive orders. 
Effective Devolution of Functionaries: 
(I) The devolution of functionaries to the Panchayati Raj Institutions 
should be patterned on the activity mapping of activities related to devolved 
functions; 
(II) Where the devolved activity requires the deputation of State 
Government officials to assist the el ected PRI in planning or implementing 
the devolved activity, the officials conc erned must be primarily responsible 
to, and under the disciplinary supervision and control of, the elected 
authority; 
(III) With a view to building a cadre  of officials and technocrats 
specialized in the devolved functions  of the PRIs, State Governments/UT 
Administrations may consider instituting a Panchayati Raj Administrative 
and Technical Service, with the State Government discontinuing further 
recruitment of staff to State services for such devolved functions; 
(IV) (i) Reconceiving the role of Dist rict Rural Development Agencies 
(DRDAs) as an important instrument for Panchayati Raj development 
through the progressive merger of DRDAs with the District Panchayats. The 
technical expertise and other facilities of the DRDAs should become 
133 

RAJYA SABHA [15 March, 2005] 
available to all tiers of the PRIs under the overall responsibility and 
disciplinary control of the elected authority in the PRIs at the appropriate 
level; 
(ii) The activities of the reconceived DRDAs with respect to the three tiers 
of the Panchayati Raj System should be patterned on the activity map for the 
devolution of functions, functionaries and funds so that all the three tiers of 
PRIs have equitable access to the resources, expertise, facilities and 
manpower of the DRDAs. 
Effective Devolution of Finances: 
(I) The "sound finances" of the Panchayats is a Constitutional 
obligation enjoined on the States by Article 243-I. In pursuance of this 
Constitutional obligation, the States and the Centre, in a true spirit of fiscal 
federalism, should work together to strengthen the finances of the elected 
local bodies; 
(II) To this end, the devolution of finances to the three tiers of the 
Panchayati Raj System should be patterned on activity mapping for the 
devolution of functions and functionaries, thus securing effective devolution 
of powers to the PRIs through the linking of the devolution of finances to the 
devolution of functions  and functionaries; 
(III) On the basis of the principles  adumbrated above, the State 
Governments might attempt to prepare a road map, to be made effective as 
soon as possible, and, in any case, by the end of the text fiscal year 2005-06, 
which might include the following components: 
(i)    Devolution, tier-wise and based on activity mapping, of: 
(a) Planning; 
(b) Budgeting; 
(c) Provisioning of finances. 
(ii)   Inclusion of a PRI component in the budget of each State/Central 
Government department based on activity mapping; 
(iii)  Provision of progressively larger untied funds, tier-wise, to the 
Panchayats by State/Central governments; 
(iv)  Provision of untied grants from the Planning Commission to the 
PRIs, tier-wise, based on activity mapping; 
134 

 
[15 March, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
(v) Tier-wise allocations, based on activity mapping of the PRIs, of 
hitherto unallocated grants, if any, made by previous Finance 
Commissions, and a pre-determined pattern for the tier-wise 
allocation within a time bound fram ework of grants from the 12th 
and future Finance Commissions; 
(vi) A schedule, to be determin ed by each State Government/UT 
Administration, of the time-frames within which State Finance 
Commissions should prepare their reports; for the submission of 
State Finance Commission recommendations, along with Action 
Taken Report (ATRs), to the Legislature; and for the executive to 
act on recommendations/ATRs endorsed by the State Legislature; 
(vii) Steps to encourage PRIs to ra ise their own resources, especially 
through the provision to "appropriate" revenues raised by them for 
their own purposes (Article 243-H). 
Gram Sabhas: 
(I) Article 243-A of Part IX of the Constitution provides for the 
establishment of Gram Sabhas to "exe rcise such powers and perform such 
functions at the village level as the Legislature of a State may, be law, 
provide"; 
(II) A strong system of Gram Sabhas is the indispensable foundation of 
good governance through Panchayati Raj; 
(III) Based on the two principles st ated above, State Governments may 
review the extent legislation to determine the legislative and other steps 
which remain to be taken to ensure that the "powers" and "functions" 
mentioned in Article 243A of the Cons titution are adequately incorporated 
in the State legislation. In particular, the following points may be examined: 
(i) The need for constituting Sabhas below the Gram level (such as Gram 
Sansad, Upa-Gram Sabha or Ward Sabha, by whatever name called) 
with the aim of ensuring that the adult population in each ward is 
given the opportunity of conveying to the Gram Sabha their views 
on issues coming up for considera tion as also holding the elected 
Ward representative responsible to the adult p opulation in each 
Ward; 
(ii)   The periodicity of meetings of Gram Sabhas and Ward Sabhas; 
(iii) Provision for full and satisfact ory consultation with special or 
disadvantaged categories of the population, such as women, SC/ ST, 
landless labourer etc;

women of a Ward/Gram Panchayat Area, to deliberate upon, and

(v) Endowing the Gram/Ward Sabha with meaningful empowerment 
through such measures as: 
(a) Right/entitlement to all the information required for the Gram/

well as to make the elected Panchayat truly answerable to the

and Andhra Pradesh. The price of ethanol aiso rose significantly at all

vide GSR 705(E) dated 27.10.2004 that five percent ethanol-blended petrol, 
148

as per Bureau of Indian Standards specifications, shall be sold in notified 
States and Union Territories if the pri ce of sourcing indigenous ethanol for

ethanol for alternative uses and the delivery price of ethanol at the location is 
comparable to the import parity price of petrol at that location and the 
indigenous ethanol industry is able to maintain the availability of ethanol for

Sindhu Water Agreement, 1960 between India and Pakistan 
†1528. SHRIMATI SUKHBUNS KAUR: 
SHRI DHARAM PAL SABHARWAL: 
DR. ALLADI P. RAJKUMAR: 
SHRI KALRAJ MISHRA: 
SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI: 
SHRI AMAR SINGH: 
SHRI KARNENDU BHATTACHARJEE: 
SHRI NAND KISHORE YADAV: 
DR. M.A.M. RAMASWAMY: 
SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA: 
Will the Minister of WATER RESOURCES be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of main conditions of the Sindhu Water Agreement, 1960 
signed between India and Pakistan under the arbitration of the World Bank; 
(b) whether it is a fact that considerin g this project as wrong project and 
against the above Agreement, Pakistan  is not agreeing to the Bagalihar 
Hydro-power Project at the river Chinab which is for the development of 
Jammu and Kashmir and is considering for soliciting the intervention of the 
World Bank; and 
(c) if so, what is Government's reaction thereto? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER 
RESOURCES (SHRI JAI PRAKASH NARAYAN YADAV): (a) The Indus 
Waters Treaty 1960, negotiated under the auspices of the World Bank, fixes 
and delimits the rights and obligations of India and Pakistan in relation to 
each other concerning the use of the waters of the indus system of rivers for 
attaining the most complete and satisfactory utilisation of its 
†Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 
176 

[15 March, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
waters, in a sprit of goodwill and friendship. U nder the Treaty, the waters of 
the Eastern Rivers viz. The Sutlej. the Beas and the Ravi (about 33 Million 
Acre Feet or 41 Billion Cubic Metres) stand allocated to India and those of 
the Western Rivers viz. The Indus, The Jhelum and The Chenab (about 135 
Million Acre Feet or 166 Billion Cubi c Metres) are to be received by 
Pakistan for their unrestricted use except for Domestic/Non-Consumptive 
Use and specified/restricted Agricu ltural Use, hydro-electric power 
generation and storage of waters by India. 
(b) Under the provisions of the Treaty, India is permitted to construct 
Run-of-River Hydroelectric Plants on  the Western Rivers conforming to 
certain design & operation criteria specified in th e Treaty. The Baglihar 
Project is one such Run-of-River Hydr oelectric Project. Pakistan has been 
expressing that the design of the 450 MW Baglihar Project in J&K violates 
certain provisions of the Treaty and has approached the World Bank on the 
15th January, 2005 for the appointment of a Neutral Expert expressing that 
differences have arisen. 
(c) India has been explaining to Pakistan that the design of the Plant fully 
conforms to the provisions of the Treaty and its objections could be amicably 
settled through detailed technical discussions, which had already indicated 
scope of narrowing down of issues. After Pakistan's aforesaid request to the 
World Bank, India has submitted to the Bank that the situation envisaged in 
the Treaty for recourse to the Bank to make a valid appointment of a Neutral 
Expert has yet not arisen and accordingly, the Bank should refrain from 
making such an appointment leaving the parties to settle remaining issues 
through mutual cooperative discussions in good faith or otherwise in 
accordance with the procedure prescribed in the Treaty.

carried out by the Central Ground Water Board (CGWB), under the Ministry 
of Water Resources, ground water in major parts of the country is by and

pockets in some parts of the country. Water being a State subject, it is

primarily the responsibility of the concerned State Governments to take 
measures to prevent pollution of ground water and to formulate schemes to

awareness programmes to educate th e people for the purpose. The CGWB 
also monitors ground water quality periodically to map the changes in it and 
apprises the State Governments of the same for taking necessary remedial 
measures. It has also drilled exploratory wells tapping contamination free 
aquifer zones and has handed over these wells to the State Governments for

States for tackling water quality proble ms in rural areas through a Centrally

Increasing Inter-State Water Disputes 
1532. SHRI T.T.V. DHINAKARAN : Will the Minister of WATER 
RESOURCES be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that the inter-state river water disputes have 
increased in the past and finding a negotiated solution has become difficult; 
(b) whether Government are aware that  such disputes affect national 
interest in several areas such as irri gation, agricultural production, drinking 
water, electricity generation, flood control, etc.; and 
(c) the steps Government propose to solve this vexed issue? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER 
RESOURCES (SHRI JAI PRAKASH NARAYAN YADAV): (a) to (c) Most 
of the major rivers in India are inter- State in character having catchments/ 
watersheds in two or more States. Often water disputes arise amongst the 
basin States with regard to the use, distribution or control of the waters in 
respect of these inter-state rivers/river valleys or in the interpretation of the 
terms of any agreement relating to the use, distribution or control of 
180 

[15 March, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
such water or in the implementation of any such agreement. River water 
dispute affect the development of Water Resources projects in such river 
basin States. As per the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956, the water 
dispute arises among two or more State Government when the Central 
Government receives complaints under Section 3 of the Act from any of the 
basin State with regard to existence of water dispute. When the Central 
Government is satisfied that the dispute cannot be settled by negotiations, the 
same is referred to a tribunal under the provisions of Inter State River Water 
Disputes Act, 1956. Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956 has been 
amended in the year 2002 whereby the adjudication of the water dispute by 
the Tribunal has been made time bound. 
Availability of Drinking Water 
†1533. SHRI KALRAJ MISHRA: Will the Minister of WATER 
RESOURCES be pleased to state: 
(a) whether per capita average drinking water is available in adequate 
quantity; and 
(b) whether this can be achieved by linking rivers of the country? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER 
RESOURCES (SHRI JAl PRAKASH NARAYAN YADAV): (a) and (b) The 
requirement of water for various sectors including domestic water has been 
assessed by the National Commission for Integrated Water Resources 
Development Plan for Diverse Uses in the Country. According to the report 
of the National Commission, the projected domestic water requirement for 
year 2025 and 2050 and 62 and 111 Billion Cubic Meter (BCM) respectively, 
which is a relatively smaller percentage of overall availability of utilizable 
water resources in the country i.e. 1112 BCM. However, there are 
considerable spatial and temporal variations in the availability of water. 
National Perspective Plan for water resources development envisages inter-
basic transfer of water which will help in reducing the regional imbalances in 
the availability of water and will also accrue benefits of drinking water 
supply in addition to other benefits Due emphasis has been laid on 
development of water resources, particularly for providing drinking water to 
all sections including urban and rural areas in the National Common 
Minimum Programme. In the National Water Policy, 2002, the drinking 
water needs of human beings and animals has been given the first charge on 
any available water and drinking water has been allocated the first priority in 
the planning and operations of water resources systems.

dated 31.12.1981 among the Chief Ministers of Punjab, Haryana and 
Rajasthan on sharing of surplus Ravi-Beas waters provided that until such 
time as Rajasthan is in a position to utilise its full share, Punjab shall be free 
to utilize the waters surplus to Rajasthan's requirements. 
(b) As per Government of Rajasthan, water utilised during 1999-2000 was 
9.173 Million Acre Feet (MAF), water requirement for new area opened for 
irrigation in Indira Gandhi Nahar Project from 1999 to 2002 is 0.54 MAF and 
thus Rajasthan is in a position to utilise its full share of 9.71 MAF (i.e. 8.6 
MAF under the agreement and pre-partition share of 1.11 MAF).

issue among the States at an opportune  time and accordingly request Bhakra 
Beas Management Board.

Agree ments Act, 2004 terminating a ll agreements on Ravi-Beas waters, 
including the 1981 agreement. A Presidential Reference in the matter is 
before the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India. Its outcome could clarify the 
position of the agreement after which the concerned States could amicably 
settle the issue.
